## Codex Review (GPT-5.4)

This PR is a bug-fix for interrupted `Calendar.Viewport` month transitions. I reviewed the full branch against a freshly fetched `upstream/master`, checked the animation/remount path, and did not find any remaining blocking issues after the added regression coverage.

### 1. Bugs / Issues (None)

No branch-relevant correctness, regression, or coverage issues remain after the current patch.

### 2. Root Cause & Patch Assessment

| Area | Assessment | Notes |
|------|:----------:|-------|
| Root cause coverage | Good | The fix addresses DOM reuse across month changes, which is the part that prevented the entering month from reapplying its starting styles on interruption |
| Patch scope | Good | The change is narrow to `Calendar.Viewport` and does not alter the month-button behavior itself |

### 3. Pattern Consistency Assessment

| Area | Assessment | Notes |
|------|:----------:|-------|
| Viewport behavior | Good | Remounting the entering content on identity changes matches the existing popup viewport pattern used elsewhere in the repo |
| API impact | Low risk | No public props or docs surface changed |

### 4. Simplification Opportunities

No further simplification changes look necessary. The month-keyed remount is small, direct, and easier to reason about than adding more transition bookkeeping around the existing node reuse path.

### 5. Edge Cases Worth Noting

| Edge case | Status | Notes |
|-----------|:------:|-------|
| Rapid repeated month changes | Covered by design | The current month subtree now remounts on visible-month changes |
| Press-and-hold navigation | Low risk | Existing increment-button coverage stayed green after the viewport change |

### 6. Test Coverage Assessment

| Validation | Status | Notes |
|------------|:------:|-------|
| `pnpm test:jsdom CalendarViewport --no-watch` | Passed | New regression test |
| `pnpm test:chromium CalendarViewport --no-watch` | Passed | Browser-targeted confirmation for the viewport change |
| `pnpm test:jsdom CalendarIncrementMonth --no-watch` | Passed | Regression check for press-and-hold navigation |
| `pnpm typescript` | Passed | No type regressions observed |
| `pnpm eslint packages/react/src/calendar/viewport/CalendarViewport.tsx packages/react/src/calendar/viewport/CalendarViewport.test.tsx` | Passed | Touched files lint clean |

### Merge Confidence Score

| Dimension | Score | Notes |
|-----------|:-----:|-------|
| Correctness | 4/5 | Root cause and affected path look well-covered |
| Regression risk | 4/5 | Scope is narrow and adjacent month-button coverage stayed green |
| Test coverage | 4/5 | Targeted JSDOM and Chromium checks both passed |

Overall merge confidence is 4/5. I would be comfortable merging this draft once normal reviewer sign-off is in place.

performed_via_github_app.description:
Publish incredibly high performance websites and applications right from GitHub. The Netlify platform connects your repositories to an all-in-one workflow for global CDN deployment, continuous integration, and automatic (and free) HTTPS. Each time you commit changes, Netlify builds your site, prerenders markup, and optimizes assets on dedicated build infrastructure. Easily create an entirely automated workflows for your web applications

## Features

### Push your site live, directly from GitHub
Deploy your site to an ultra-redundant global CDN that’s purpose built for serving pages and assets quickly and consistently.

### Automate deployment
Netlify’s built-in Continuous Deployment automatically runs your build commands and deploys the result whenever you push to your Git repository.

### Add a custom domain
Purchase domains and manage DNS zones and records right inside of Netlify.

### HTTPS is automatic
Your site will automatically be secured with a free TLS certificate from Let’s Encrypt.

### Deploy Previews
Netlify’s Deploy Previews streamlined your workflow by giving you a unique, permanent URL to check what your changes will be like in production whenever you submit a pull request.

### And a lot more!
Netlify includes solutions for forms, identity, and even custom functions powered by AWS Lambda. And all this functionality can be configured directly in your repo.
